subject: Operator bundle rotation and image attestation for air-gapped deployments

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Operator bundle rotation and image attestation for air-gapped deployments

Hi Diana,

Thanks again for the time last week. As we prep the Private deployment package for your air-gapped clusters, I want to align on two operational pieces that have tripped other customers: (1) how you plan to rotate update bundles and (2) how images in the offline bundle are signed/verified by operators.

High level ask: can you confirm your operator team's current constraints for receiving and applying offline bundles? Specifically: allowed media (USB, DVD, secure transfer appliance), maximum bundle size, and whether you require hardware-backed signing (HSM) or will accept software attestation (cosign/TUF).

We have a proposed minimal workflow at our end (below) but don't want to dictate until we understand your constraints. If you can send any internal spec or an example bundle, that would be extremely helpful.

Jonas
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Diana Ortiz <diana.ortiz@nebula-labs.com>

Cc: ops@nebula-labs.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator bundle rotation and image attestation for air-gapped deployments

Jonas —

Thanks for the note. Short answers first: we primarily use downloadable physical media (secure USB shuttle) and an internal courier for large sites. Max bundle size today is ~8GB per site due to the USB protocol and our import tooling. We prefer hardware-backed signing (HSM) for production clusters but will accept signed artifacts from a software key for staging.

Attached is a sanitized copy of our current bundle layout and a small example: nebula_update_bundle_spec.tar.gz (contains manifest, images, operator hooks). We also added a short list of requirements: offline verification must be possible without reaching any external PKI endpoints during install.

Questions for Redwood: do you produce a single monolithic image per release or a multi-image bundle with layer manifests? Also, do you provide tooling for offline key rotation / automated verification on the operator machine?

—Diana
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Nebula Labs
(attachment: nebula_update_bundle_spec.tar.gz, 18KB)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Diana Ortiz <diana.ortiz@nebula-labs.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator bundle rotation and image attestation for air-gapped deployments

Diana — thanks for the spec. I reviewed nebula_update_bundle_spec.tar.gz and sketched an operator-focused workflow that maps to both your staging and prod constraints. Summary below and full draft attached (operator-workflow-draft.md).

Proposed operator bundle workflow (high level):
- At build time (Redwood): generate a release bundle containing a set of container images, a top-level manifest.json, and an operator-install hook directory.
- Signatures: we produce two signatures per image: (1) an ephemeral release signature (software key) and (2) an optional HSM-backed attestation for customers that provide an external signing endpoint. Both signatures are included in the bundle alongside a root_of_trust.json.
- Distribution: bundle is exported as a compressed tarball with integrity checksum (SHA256). Size controls: we can split bundles into numbered chunks (part-01.tar.gz, part-02.tar.gz) to respect the 8GB limit and provide a small chunking manifest to reassemble on the operator host.
- Operator-side verification: a small single-binary verifier (offline_verifier) runs entirely on the operator host: it verifies checksums, validates signatures against the provided root_of_trust.json, and runs a configurable policy (allowlist of keys, timestamp window, revocation list file shipped in bundle). No external network calls required.

Attachments included: operator-workflow-draft.md, image-attestation-example.json (sample attestation payload and verification commands).

Open questions for Nebula:
1) Do your operator hosts have a TPM or HSM we can use to seal ephemeral keys?
2) If you require HSM signing, do you prefer Redwood to sign using our HSM in a hosted provisioning step, or to accept a customer-provided public key that we include in root_of_trust.json?

If useful I can record a 20-minute demo of the verifier and chunk reassembly for your SREs.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
(attachments: operator-workflow-draft.md, image-attestation-example.json)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Diana Ortiz <diana.ortiz@nebula-labs.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator bundle rotation and image attestation for air-gapped deployments

Diana / team —

I reviewed the draft workflow and have a few security-focused items we should lock down before production:

1) Root of trust and key lifecycle: include an explicit root rotation plan in operator-workflow-draft.md. For HSM-backed customers, we must ship a public key fingerprint and a signed key-rotation manifest that the operator verifies.
2) Timestamping and replay protection: include a monotonically increasing bundle sequence number and require operator to reject out-of-order bundles unless explicit force flag is set (logged and audited).
3) Verification tooling: the offline_verifier should support cosign-compatible verification and a small TUF-style metadata layer so we can revoke images without contacting external servers. We can keep metadata local in the bundle and support a signed ad-hoc revocation list.
4) Audit logs: operator must produce a signed audit log of install events (hash of bundle + operator ID + timestamp) that can be exported during a periodic review.

I'll add an example key-rotation snippet to operator-workflow-draft.md and a short checklist for security review. Also recommend adding an internal test harness for your SREs to run bundle verification in a CI step before handing to the courier.

Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Operator bundle rotation and image attestation for air-gapped deployments

Diana / team —

Great progress, thanks everyone. Quick summary and next steps so we have clear owners:

Decisions agreed:
- Redwood will produce multi-image bundles with a chunking manifest to respect the 8GB limit.
- We will ship both a software-signed attestation for staging and support HSM-backed signatures for production; root_of_trust.json will contain the public keys/fingerprints.
- Offline verifier (single binary) will implement cosign-compatible checks, local TUF-style metadata, and produce a signed audit log.

Action items and owners:
- Ava: finalize operator-workflow-draft.md with chunk reassembly commands and upload example verifier binary (deadline: 2026-05-25).
- Mina: add key-rotation manifest template and a short security checklist for operator acceptance tests (deadline: 2026-05-22).
- Nebula (Diana): confirm whether operator hosts have TPM/HSM or if Redwood should provide HSM signing (reply by 2026-05-21). Also confirm if the courier accepts multi-part bundles.

I've attached the HubSpot deal link and a working Drive doc (see related_links) where we'll keep the final artifacts. If Nebula is OK, I'll create a short demo slot next week (20m) for your SREs to watch the verifier run against your sample bundle.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this into NB-4521.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
